node.statement: For any endomorphism T of a finite-dimensional real normed space with ||T+I||<1, set B=(T+I)/2. Then ||B||<1/2, every I-tB is invertible for 0<=t<=1 by the Neumann series, and continuity of the nonzero real determinant along t gives det(I-B)>0 from det(I)=1. Since I-T=2(I-B), det(I-T)=2^d det(I-B)>0, where d is the real dimension. Applying this to T=D-breve-sigma_{breve-e} yields det(I-D-breve-sigma_{breve-e})>0 (and in particular nonzero).
